Name that ticket. content.content:
Two things I left out of the mail this morning.

1. The level editor (Assets/Scripts/LevelEditor and the LevelDesigner panels), anything in an Editor folder and the debug menu (Assets/Scripts/Debug) are stripped before we ship to players on iOS and Android. A ticket whose changes are only level editor or debug tooling never reached players, Done or not.

2. For the rules tab: the starting tier check in the code is cpm > 90, not >= 90, and it runs when a player's 10th game ends, wins and losses both counted, not after 10 levels cleared. ZOM-199 says >= 90 after the first 10 levels, but the code never changed from the original spec, so 90 exactly stays on tier 0.

Blake

content.content: {"result":"{\"id\": \"ZOM-42\", \"uuid\": null, \"identifier\": \"ZOM-42\", \"number\": 42, \"title\": \"Dynamic Difficulty\", \"description\": \"# **Part 1:**\\n\\nAllow level editor to create tiered version of each level. Tier 0 is default. Then we have -2, -1, 0, +1, +2 tiers. (Or more if designer creates it, but each level should have a minimum of these 5 tiers, rest are optional)\\n\\nWhat's identical across tiers, this is to ensure code consistency across all tiers and keeping code simplified.\\n\\n* List of items in the level. (For lower level tiers we can set qty to 0 to effectively not have any)\\n* List of monsters in the level (For lower level tiers we can set qty to 0 to effectively not have any)\\n\\nWhat's not identical in the tiers:\\n\\n* Quantity of the items\\n* Quantity of the monsters\\n* Pre-warm period\\n\\nPlayers starts at default tier 0, but gets assigned after the first 6-7 levels based on CPM, to be defined later, and gets moved up and down based on certain winning/losing conditions.\\n\\nDemotion Rules based on win streak:\\n\\n1. Use CPM data to place player in a starting tier. (1st 10 level avg CPM > 90 (top 20%) moves to tier 1, rest stays in tier 0)\\n2. Lose 4 in a row, you're demoted.\\n\\nPromotion Rules based on win record of last 10 attempts:\\n\\n1. Tier -2 is an exception. You promote instantly after 1 win if you're in tier -2.\\n2. Starting at tier -1, we evaluate UP TO THE MOST RECENT 10 attempts of the player\\n3. We promote if if win rate is 80% or higher. This means we constantly look at the last 10 games played, if at any time win rate is 80%+, we promote. This also means it is possible to be promoted by simply winning 8 games in a row, without playing the full 10 games. {"id": "ZOM-42", "uuid": null, "identifier": "ZOM-42", "number": 42, "title": "Dynamic Difficulty", "description": "# **Part 1:**

Allow level editor to create tiered version of each level. Tier 0 is default. Then we have -2, -1, 0, +1, +2 tiers. (Or more if designer creates it, but each level should have a minimum of these 5 tiers, rest are optional)

What's identical across tiers, this is to ensure code consistency across all tiers and keeping code simplified.

* List of items in the level. (For lower level tiers we can set qty to 0 to effectively not have any)
* List of monsters in the level (For lower level tiers we can set qty to 0 to effectively not have any)

What's not identical in the tiers:

* Quantity of the items
* Quantity of the monsters
* Pre-warm period

Players starts at default tier 0, but gets assigned after the first 6-7 levels based on CPM, to be defined later, and gets moved up and down based on certain winning/losing conditions.

Demotion Rules based on win streak:

1. Use CPM data to place player in a starting tier. (1st 10 level avg CPM > 90 (top 20%) moves to tier 1, rest stays in tier 0)
2. Lose 4 in a row, you're demoted.

Promotion Rules based on win record of last 10 attempts:

1. Tier -2 is an exception. You promote instantly after 1 win if you're in tier -2.
2. Starting at tier -1, we evaluate UP TO THE MOST RECENT 10 attempts of the player
3. We promote if if win rate is 80% or higher. This means we constantly look at the last 10 games played, if at any time win rate is 80%+, we promote. This also means it is possible to be promoted by simply winning 8 games in a row, without playing the full 10 games. We call this "early exit" because you're mathematically guaranteed to win 80%.

Demotion Rules based on win record of last 10 attempts:

1. Similar to promotion rules, we demote someone when their win rate for up to the last 10 games is 50% or lower.
2. Early exits is also possible. Meaning that if you manage to avoid the 4 losing streak demotion, you can still get demoted by doing LLLWLL or LWLWLLL or LLWLLL, these are some cases where you didn't play the full 10 games, but is mathematically guaranteed to finish at 50% or lower win rate.

Please note that every time a promotion/demotion happens, the record is reset and we start at 0 games played.

This also means that with a win rate of 60 or 70%, the player does not get promoted or demoted.

A losing streak of 4 games in a row can still trigger at any time, regardless of whatever record. But a demotion from this will still reset the game record for the win rate evaluation.

# **Part 2: Future expansion**

If a player manages to reach the highest tier difficulty consistently, we will implement an auto tier+ system. What this is will simply be swapping monsters in the level. Meaning we will first create a dictionary table of how we want to swap monsters. This is a sample of a table:

Monster in Max Tier Difficulty Track | Monsters to replace with

Punk A | Punk B

Punk B | Punk C

Punk C | Punk D

Punk D | Brute A

Boss 1 | Boss 3

Boss 2 | Boss 4

Boss 10 | Boss 10

If the player is winning consistently at a threshold we set, then we run this process *once* when the level starts, replacing all monsters with an upgraded one. If the player continues to excel, then we can run this process *twice* as the level starts. input.command:
cd /app; python3 -c "
import json
iss=json.load(open('p1.json'))+json.load(open('p2.json'))
done=set('23 42 45 246 254 263 274 280 288 293 295 162 163 173 200 201 202 250 277 303 312 315 276 203'.split())
ab=set(i['id'][4:] for i in iss if (i.get('assignee') or '').startswith('arthur'))
ids=sorted(set([int(i['id'][4:]) for i in iss if i['createdAt']<'2025-09-01'])|set(range(10,63)))
rest=[x for x in ids if str(x) not in done and str(x) not in ab]
print(len(rest))
n=9
for k in range(n): print(','.join('ZOM-%d'%x for x in rest[k::n]))
"

"

cd /app; python3 -c "
import json,re
prs=json.load(open('prs.json'))
for p in sorted(prs,key=lambda p:p['number']):
  txt=(p['title'] or '')+' '+(p.get('body') or '')+' '+p['head']['ref']
  m=set(re.findall(r'zom[^0-9a-z]{0,3}(\d+)',txt,re.I))
  if m: print(p['number'],p['merged'],sorted(m,key=int),'|',p['title'][:60],'|',p['head']['ref'])
"

This means by level 40, a player can easily be labeled as tier 4, which is often the case given how easy our game is early on.

However many of our levels only have 2 tiers of difficult, 0 and 1. And the idea is that if a player loses 4 in a row, they get demoted a player tier. So 4 -> 3 -> 2 and -> 1. However this creates a problem.

A player is difficulty tier 4, plays a difficulty tier 1 level, gets stuck, loses 4 in a row, they are demoted to tier 3. They still load difficulty tier 1 level, and continues to lose. A player would need to lose 12 times for them to actually get to difficulty tier 0 for that level. This defeats the whole purpose of downgrading them. Losing 12 in a row will cause a user to churn.

Solution: when a player is demoted, we also need to demote the level difficulty for the level they are currently on.

So if a player is demoted from tier 4 -> 3, and they were playing tier 1 difficulty and failed, that level will load the tier 0 version.

The following level, it will just go back to normal, meaning if a tier 3 level is available, that's the level that will load for the player. values: How it works in the store builds today (iOS 0.3.49 / Android 0.3.133)
Each level has tiered versions, -2 to +2 (more if the designer creates them); tier 0 is the default version of each level.

Checked when the player's 10th game ends (wins and losses both counted, not 10 levels cleared). Average CPM over those games > 90 starts the player on tier 1; everyone else stays on tier 0 (90 exactly stays on tier 0).
Blake's reply to the store builds mail (code check), overrides ZOM-199 / Robert's deck

Starting at tier -1, we evaluate up to the most recent 10 attempts of the player; promote if win rate is 80% or higher (early exit: 8 wins in a row promotes without playing the full 10). Tier -2 is an exception: you promote instantly after 1 win. Every promotion/demotion resets the record to 0 games played.

Lose 4 in a row, you're demoted (can trigger at any time, regardless of record). Also demoted when win rate for up to the last 10 games is 50% or lower (early exit possible, e.g. LLLWLL). Every promotion/demotion resets the record to 0 games played. A 60-70% win rate neither promotes nor demotes.

Yes. When a player is demoted, the level they are currently on also drops a difficulty tier (e.g. failing a tier 1 level loads its tier 0 version); the following level goes back to normal (player's tier, or the closest tier the level has).
Blunder (overfilling the match bar) enrages the monsters; enrage adds walk speed and damage only (HP boost switched off). Values are per monster, below.
Enrage per monster (copied from ZM monster enrage sheet, Live tab, as it stands)

Per Blake's check of the code, the starting tier check is cpm > 90 (not >= 90), and it runs when the player's 10th game ends, wins and losses both counted (not after the first 10 levels cleared). So a player at exactly 90 CPM stays on tier 0.

The difficulty baseline is in the ZM Difficulty folder: <https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1Vwwlsjc8znmoP3RkOyfasRg4YtvUC5lcJWwakYiBGDs/edit|ZM difficulty baseline register - Oct 6>. It has two tabs, Tickets and Rules in force. It's shared with everyone on the tuning invite: Robert and Brian can edit, you can comment, and Arthur can view.

**29 tickets made the list:**
• Live: 16
• Editor only: 9
• Replaced: 1
• Not shipped: 3

**Not shipped:** ZOM-202, ZOM-280, ZOM-293
**Editor only:** ZOM-162, ZOM-163, ZOM-173, ZOM-200, ZOM-201, ZOM-250, ZOM-277, ZOM-312, ZOM-315
**Replaced:** ZOM-254 was replaced by ZOM-282. That's the only one.

**Starting tier for a new player:** they get it when their 10th game ends, with wins and losses both counted, not after 10 levels cleared. If their average CPM is over 90 they start on tier 1. Everyone else stays on tier 0, including a player at exactly 90. That's what Blake found in the code. ZOM-199 and Robert's deck say >= 90 after the first 10 levels, so I commented on ZOM-199 with what the build does.

The Editor only and Not shipped tickets each have a comment naming the two builds (iOS 0.3.49 / Android 0.3.133), and ZOM-254 has one naming ZOM-282. Analytics and tutorial tickets and ZOM-258 are left off, as you asked.

The register is built, it's in the ZM Difficulty folder and shared with the Monday invite, the ticket comments are posted, and I've replied to Leonard in his DM thread ([message](https://harmonygamesgroup.slack.com/archives/D05HB64NMQU/p1759302706000000?thread_ts=1759261706.530914&cid=D05HB64NMQU)).

**The sheet:** [ZM difficulty baseline register - Oct 6](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1Vwwlsjc8znmoP3RkOyfasRg4YtvUC5lcJWwakYiBGDs/edit) has two tabs, as the session agenda asked:
- **Tickets:** 29 rows. Status counts:

  | Status | Count | Tickets |
  |---|---|---|
  | Live | 16 | |
  | Editor only | 9 | ZOM-162, 163, 173, 200, 201, 250, 277, 312, 315 |
  | Replaced | 1 | ZOM-254, replaced by ZOM-282 |
  | Not shipped | 3 | ZOM-202, 280, 293 |

  Each row also has the three columns Robert asked for: Linear assignee, done date in Pacific time and Linear priority.
- **Rules in force:**
  - **Starting tier:** taken from Blake's reply to his store builds mail, because the build and the write-ups disagree. A player's average CPM must be over 90 when their 10th game ends, wins and losses both counted, to start on tier 1. Everyone else, including exactly 90, stays on tier 0.
  - **Promotion and demotion:** worded the way ZOM-42 words them.
  - **Level drop:** yes, the level drops a tier after a demotion (from ZOM-303).
  - **Enrage:** your monster enrage sheet's Live tab copied as it stands. Mailman, Mayor2 and PartyGirl are marked "not copied yet".

**Scope:**
- **Title matches:** "attack power" counts, per Leonard's comment on the card.
- **Added:** ZOM-221, 281, 300, 305 and 378, because Blake's closing notes on them start with "tiers:".
- **Left off:**
  - the analytics and tutorial tickets Leonard listed;
  - ZOM-258, the enraged icon;
  - the two duplicates.
- **"Not tiers":** I checked every match3d PR (477) and none has a Blake review saying "not tiers", so nothing dropped out under that rule.

**Sharing:** Leonard left three instructions that change the card's rules, and I followed all of them. Brian got edit along with Robert (from the card's checklist), Arthur got view only (from Leonard's "notes for monday" doc), and Leonard has comment access.

**Ticket comments:** ZOM-199 got one saying what the build actually does. ZOM-254 got one naming ZOM-282. The 12 Editor only and Not shipped tickets each got one saying the change isn't in iOS 0.3.49 or Android 0.3.133, which follows the checklist update to the card's rule 6. No other tickets were touched and none were created.

**Judgement calls to be aware of:**
- **Editor only vs Live:** Linear and GitHub only link a handful of PRs to these tickets, so for most I went on the ticket text and Blake's closing notes. If one gets questioned on Monday, the likeliest is ZOM-263 (the ricochet attack power fix): I marked it Live because it fixes the card-profile attack power players see.
- **Trello checklist:** I left the two "Before Monday" items unticked on Leonard's card.
